primals.name: Front shoulder
primals.summary: Hang it by the shank. The shoulder blade is a flat bone with a raised ridge down its outside face; the ridge splits the two best cuts.
landmarks: Blade ridge: a hard raised line on the outside face of the shoulder blade. Run a finger along it, then slice along it down to bone.
Blade cartilage: the pale, rubbery edge at the top of the blade (at the bottom when hung by the shank). It is NOT a brisket flap.
Elbow joint: bend the leg to find it; the shank is below it.

primals.name: Backstrap (loin)
primals.summary: The long muscle on each side of the spine, outside the ribs. The best steaks on the animal.
landmarks: Runs from the hip to the shoulder along the top of the spine. Remove whole along the spine and the rib tops, then trim silver skin.

primals.name: Tenderloin
primals.summary: Inside the body cavity under the spine, in front of the hips. Small and the most tender; easy to lose if the carcass is quartered without gutting.
landmarks: Inside the cavity, pressed under the spine just ahead of the pelvis. Peel out by hand and knife tip.

primals.name: Ribs, flank and neck
primals.summary: Thin, sinewy meat. Usually trimmed to grind; the neck can also be a whole braising roast.
landmarks: Rib meat lies between and over the ribs; flank is the thin belly wall.

primals.name: Hindquarter
primals.summary: The biggest quarter. Separate it into its natural muscle groups along the seams around the femur, then trim each group.
landmarks: Femur: the big leg bone through the middle. Every round muscle seams off around it.
Knee joint (stifle): the sirloin tip (knuckle) sits on the front of the femur just above it.
Hip end (ball joint): the top sirloin sits over it.

cuts.name: Brisket and rib flaps
cuts.find: Thin red flaps hanging off the bottom and front of a shoulder hung by the shank: brisket and rib meat left attached when it was quartered. They are red meat and floppy. The pale, stiff, rubbery edge on the blade is cartilage; leave it on the blade.
steps: Pull a flap out so it hangs tight.
Find the seam where the thin flap meets the thick shoulder muscle.
Cut along that seam until the flap comes free.
Repeat for each flap.
Lay them flat; keep any brisket thicker than about 1 inch whole, the rest goes in the grind bag.

cuts.name: Flat iron
cuts.find: Outside face of the blade, on one side of the blade ridge (the larger side).
steps: Slice along the blade ridge down to the bone.
Work the knife flat against the blade and lift the muscle off.
Lay it flat. A thick gristle seam runs down its middle.
Peel the muscle off the gristle from each side, giving two flat steaks.

cuts.name: Mock tender
cuts.find: Outside face of the blade, on the other side of the blade ridge (the smaller, cone-shaped muscle).
steps: From the ridge cut, work the knife flat against the blade on the other side.
Lift the whole cone-shaped muscle off.

cuts.name: Clod
cuts.find: The big muscle mass in the angle behind the arm bone, between the blade and the elbow.
steps: Find the arm bone (humerus) under it.
Keep the knife against the bone and work the whole muscle off.
Split along natural seams into roasts, or cube it.
cuts.pack: 2-3 lb roasts or 1 lb stew packs

cuts.name: Fore shank
steps: Bend the leg to find the elbow joint.
Cut through the joint.
Keep whole (or saw into cross-cut rounds) for braising, or strip the meat for grind.
cuts.pack: Whole shank, or into the grind bag

cuts.name: Shoulder trim
cuts.find: Everything left on the inside face of the blade and the bones.
steps: Strip the remaining meat off the blade and bones.
Remove silver skin and blood-shot meat.

cuts.name: Backstrap steaks (filet-style)
steps: Trim all silver skin.
Cut across the grain into 1-1.5 in medallions.

cuts.name: Backstrap roast
cuts.find: Thick center sections of the backstrap.
steps: Leave 1 lb sections whole.

cuts.name: Backstrap trim
steps: Collect ends and edges while trimming.

cuts.name: Tenderloin
cuts.find: Inside the cavity under the spine.
steps: Peel out whole.
Trim silver skin.
Leave whole or cut medallions.

cuts.name: Rib and flank trim
cuts.find: Between and over the ribs; the belly wall.
steps: Fillet the meat off the rib cage.
Trim fat and membrane.

cuts.name: Neck
cuts.find: Between the head and the shoulders.
steps: Bone it out for grind, or saw it into a whole bone-in braising roast.

cuts.name: Top round
cuts.find: The large muscle on the inside of the leg.
steps: Open the natural seam on the inside of the leg.
Follow it around and lift the muscle off the femur.

cuts.name: Bottom round
cuts.find: The outside/back of the leg, behind the femur.
steps: Seam it off the femur along the back of the leg.
Separate the eye of round from it along the seam.

cuts.name: Eye of round
cuts.find: A long cylinder attached to the bottom round.
steps: Separate from the bottom round along the seam.

cuts.name: Sirloin tip
cuts.find: The football-shaped muscle on the front of the femur just above the knee.
steps: Cut along the seams on each side down to the femur.
Lift it off the bone.

cuts.name: Top sirloin
cuts.find: Over the hip at the top of the quarter, where the backstrap ended.
steps: Seam it off the pelvis and hip joint.

cuts.name: Hind shank
steps: Cut through the knee joint.
Keep whole for braising or strip for grind.

cuts.name: Hindquarter trim
cuts.find: Everything left on the bones and the edges of the big muscles.
steps: Strip all remaining meat.
Remove silver skin and blood-shot meat.
